subject.title: Gmail hook delivery verification fails even when message tool uses Telegram target

question: For a hook with no resolved runner-owned recipient, should a successful explicit `message` tool send be recorded as the run’s delivery, or must the hook require an explicit configured delivery target (or disabled runner delivery)?
rationale: Current main intentionally refuses keyless inherited targets to avoid sending or replaying into the wrong conversation, while the reporter has demonstrated a real successful direct-send side effect followed by an error status.

options.title: Keep strict planned-target verification
options.body: Require hook mappings that use announce delivery to specify a resolvable recipient, and document direct-send hooks as runner-delivery-disabled.

options.title: Accept explicit direct sends
options.body: Treat a successful direct message-tool send as delivery for targetless hook runs, with a narrowly scoped test that preserves the keyless `last` refusal.

recommendation.title: Keep strict planned-target verification
recommendation.body: Require hook mappings that use announce delivery to specify a resolvable recipient, and document direct-send hooks as runner-delivery-disabled.

likelyOwner.reason: The central delivery-mode and isolated-cron routing behavior traces most strongly to this feature history.
